candidates.sector_or_industry: AI accelerators, networking, accelerated computing platforms
candidates.theme_relation: NVIDIA is the central public-market mapping for AI accelerator demand and associated networking platforms, with fiscal 2025 data-center revenue evidence showing the scale of accelerated computing demand.

source_nodes: Hyperscaler AI capex and cloud compute demand
candidates.theme_relation: Microsoft converts AI software, Copilot, and model-lab demand into Azure compute utilization and upstream orders for accelerators, CPUs, networking, data-center sites, power, and leases.
TSMC is a core manufacturing chokepoint for AI accelerator wafers and advanced packaging technologies needed to integrate compute die, HBM, interposers, and chip-stacking architectures.

source_nodes: Hyperscaler AI capex and cloud compute demand
candidates.theme_relation: AWS is a primary buyer and operator of AI data-center infrastructure, pulling through chips, servers, networking, power, and data-center construction while also developing Trainium and Inferentia.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Cloud hyperscaler / AI infrastructure and model platform
source_nodes: Hyperscaler AI capex and cloud compute demand
candidates.theme_relation: Alphabet links Gemini demand, Google Cloud AI infrastructure, TPUs, GPUs, data-center construction, and energy infrastructure into a vertically integrated AI compute demand signal.
SK hynix is one of the three major HBM suppliers and maps directly to the AI memory-bandwidth chokepoint created by accelerator demand.

source_nodes: Hyperscaler AI capex and cloud compute demand
candidates.theme_relation: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is a fast-growing AI compute platform whose large AI-related RPO can pull through GPUs, data-center leases, networking, and power infrastructure.

source_nodes: Hyperscaler AI capex and cloud compute demand
candidates.theme_relation: CoreWeave is a direct AI compute capacity provider whose backlog, contracted power, and GPU-backed infrastructure make it a clean signal for outsourced AI cloud demand, with financing and concentration risks requiring later validation.

candidates.sector_or_industry: AI platform / social media / hyperscale infrastructure
source_nodes: Hyperscaler AI capex and cloud compute demand
candidates.theme_relation: Meta is a major AI infrastructure buyer whose model training, inference, recommendation, and generative AI workloads translate into high data-center, server, and infrastructure hardware demand.

Samsung is one of the three major HBM suppliers and remains a critical potential swing supplier for AI memory availability, though customer qualification and allocation evidence needs deeper validation.
Micron is one of the three major HBM suppliers and maps to memory-bandwidth scarcity in AI accelerator systems.
Modine supplies mission-critical cooling systems to data-center and hyperscale customers, making it a direct beneficiary if AI rack densities keep increasing cooling intensity.
Digital Realty maps AI demand into scarce data-center capacity, interconnection-rich sites, signed leases, and backlog of powered infrastructure.
Bloom Energy maps to the regulated-input power chokepoint by providing onsite fuel-cell capacity that can reduce dependence on delayed grid interconnections for AI and cloud infrastructure.
Comfort Systems is a second-order AI capex beneficiary if time-to-data-center and skilled mechanical/electrical construction capacity remain chokepoints.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Electrical connection, protection, enclosures, liquid-cooling infrastructure
candidates.theme_relation: nVent supplies liquid-cooling and power/enclosure infrastructure around AI racks, benefiting from rising rack density and more complex data-center power and cooling architectures.

candidates.sector_or_industry: High-speed connectivity semiconductors / active electrical cables
candidates.theme_relation: Credo maps to AI cluster networking constraints through active electrical cables and high-speed connectivity products used in hyperscale and AI data-center networks.
Applied Digital maps to power-secured AI campus development and long-duration contracted colocation revenue, with financing, tenant, and construction-delivery risks requiring deeper validation.

coverage_gaps: The current merged universe remains U.S.-heavy. Layer 2 should add Taiwan, Korea, Japan, Europe, China A-share/H-share, and India public-market mappings for memory, equipment, substrates, power equipment, cooling, and data-center infrastructure.
Advanced-packaging equipment and materials are underrepresented. Need candidate expansion across CoWoS capacity, SoIC, hybrid bonding, substrates, interposers, inspection, test, and OSAT capacity.

AI networking and optics are underrepresented relative to likely cluster-scale bottlenecks. Need a dedicated expansion for Ethernet switching, optical DSPs, transceivers, CPO, retimers, AECs, and cabling.
Power equipment coverage is too narrow. Need regional mapping for transformers, switchgear, turbines, grid interconnection, backup power, substations, and utility exposure.

Software monetization is not yet fully mapped. Need separate coverage of enterprise AI application vendors, data platforms, observability, cybersecurity, and database layers, while separating real monetization from theme adjacency.

The universe uses pre-validation Layer 1 scoring. Later layers must verify filings, latest earnings calls, customer concentration, backlog convertibility, capex funding, margins, and valuation/pricing.

evidence.claim: IEA states that AI is accelerating deployment of high-performance accelerated servers and increasing power density in data centers; it also reports that data centers account for 2.6% of global electricity demand.
IEA's 2026 follow-up says global data-center electricity demand grew by 17% in 2025, in line with IEA projections.
evidence.source_title: IEA - Key Questions on Energy and AI, Executive Summary

evidence.claim: NVIDIA reported fiscal 2025 data-center revenue of $115.2 billion, up 142% year over year, driven by data-center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI workloads.
evidence.source_title: NVIDIA CFO Commentary on Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2025 Results

evidence.claim: TSMC's 2025 annual report states it is developing advanced packaging and 3D chip-stacking technologies including CoWoS, InFO, TSMC-SoIC, and COUPE to support AI and high-performance-computing customer needs.
Microsoft said customer demand continues to exceed supply, Q2 FY2026 capex was $37.5B, and roughly two-thirds of capex was for short-lived assets primarily GPUs and CPUs.
evidence.source_title: Microsoft Fiscal Year 2026 Second Quarter Earnings Conference Call

evidence.claim: Microsoft said it expects roughly $190B of calendar 2026 capex and expects to remain capacity constrained at least through 2026.
evidence.source_title: Microsoft Fiscal Year 2026 Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call

evidence.claim: Amazon reported AWS Q4 2025 sales of $35.6B, up 24% year over year, and said it expects about $200B of 2026 capex across Amazon due to strong demand and opportunities including AI and chips.
Alphabet said 2026 capex investments are anticipated to be in the range of $175B-$185B to meet customer demand and capitalize on opportunities ahead.
Alphabet describes Google Cloud Platform as including AI infrastructure with Cloud TPUs and GPUs.
evidence.source_title: Alphabet Investor Relations FAQs and General Information

evidence.claim: Meta raised its 2025 capital expenditure outlook to $66 billion to $72 billion, with spending tied to AI infrastructure, data centers, servers, and infrastructure hardware.
evidence.source_title: Meta to spend up to $72B on AI infrastructure in 2025 as compute arms race escalates

evidence.claim: Oracle reported fiscal 2026 Q3 RPO of $553B, up 325% year over year, and said most of the Q3 RPO increase related to large-scale AI contracts.
evidence.source_title: Oracle Announces Fiscal Year 2026 Third Quarter Financial Results

evidence.claim: Oracle reported fiscal 2026 Q3 Cloud Infrastructure revenue of $4.9B, up 84% in USD.
evidence.source_title: Oracle Announces Fiscal Year 2026 Third Quarter Financial Results

evidence.claim: CoreWeave reported Q1 2026 revenue backlog of $99.4B, surpassed 1 GW of active power, and expanded total contracted power to over 3.5 GW.
evidence.source_title: Layer 1B node-level candidate output - CoreWeave evidence

evidence.claim: Public market reporting and industry sources consistently identify SK hynix, Samsung Electronics, and Micron as the three major HBM suppliers, making HBM supply highly concentrated.
evidence.source_title: S&P Global - SK Hynix set to overtake Samsung as DRAM leader amid AI-driven memory boom

evidence.claim: A 2026 AI infrastructure taxonomy paper identifies power availability, thermal and water constraints, interconnect scaling, memory pressure, data-pipeline throughput, and lifecycle cost as cross-layer infrastructure constraints.
evidence.source_title: A Unified Metric Architecture for AI Infrastructure: A Cross-Layer Taxonomy Integrating Performance, Efficiency, and Cost

memory_update.text: The AI Layer 1 universe should remain infrastructure-stack based: cloud demand signals, accelerators, HBM, advanced packaging, foundry, AI networking, data-center power/cooling, construction, and software monetization.
Highest-priority chokepoint nodes after Layer 1C are accelerators, HBM, advanced packaging, AI data-center power, cooling, and networking.

Layer 2 should broaden non-U.S. public-market mappings and add dedicated expansions for advanced-packaging tools/materials, AI optics/networking, power equipment, and enterprise AI software monetization.

Hyperscaler capex and AI cloud backlog should be treated as demand signals, while HBM, packaging, power, cooling, and data-center construction should be treated as installation chokepoints that determine whether compute can actually be deployed.

summary: Layer 1C merged the AI theme universe from Layer 1A theme decomposition and Layer 1B node-level candidates into a deduplicated initial research universe. The highest-priority names are those with direct evidence of AI compute demand, contracted AI infrastructure capacity, or chokepoint exposure in accelerators, HBM, advanced packaging, networking, data-center power, cooling, and construction. Scores reflect Serenity relevance before valuation, market-pricing, or full evidence validation; they are not buy/sell recommendations.
universe_method: multi-step: theme decomposition -> node expansion -> dedupe/rank
